name: So
title: Egypt's Pharaoh
summary: So was an Egyptian king (pharaoh) to whom Hosea, the last king of Israel, sent messengers seeking an alliance against Assyria. This alliance failed, and Hosea's rebellion against Assyria led to the siege of Samaria and the fall of the Northern Kingdom. So is mentioned only once in the Bible, but his role is significant as background for Israel's final downfall.

keyEvents.title: Hosea's Alliance Attempt with So
keyEvents.description: Israel's King Hosea sent messengers to So, the king of Egypt, seeking military support against Assyria. This was a desperate attempt to break free from Assyrian domination.

keyEvents.title: Assyrian Reaction to the Alliance
keyEvents.description: When Assyria's King Shalmaneser discovered Hosea's betrayal and secret pact with Egypt, he imprisoned Hosea and began the siege of Samaria.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Samaria and Israel's Exile
keyEvents.description: After a three-year siege, Samaria fell in 722 BC. The population of the Northern Kingdom was deported to Assyria, marking the end of the northern kingdom of Israel.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on Israel
keyEvents.description: The Bible explains that Israel's fall was due to the people's sin and idolatry. The alliance with Egypt instead of trusting in God was part of this apostasy.

keyEvents.title: Prophetic Warning Against an Alliance with Egypt
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah repeatedly warned against relying on Egypt for military help instead of trusting in the Lord. So's inability to help Israel confirmed these warnings.
